standard.title: Tone, intonation and phrasing for fluency
standard.description: use tone-syllables and apply intonation, stress and phrasing to enhance fluency, and respond to and create texts in a range of contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students entering at Y7-8 have developed spoken target language fluency in home and community contexts, typically with regional or family accent features. They have not yet systematically examined their own pronunciation, compared it with standard forms, applied Pinyin as an analytical tool, or performed for formal or academic audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use tone-syllables, intonation, stress and phrasing to enhance fluency in responding to and creating texts across a range of contexts — including self-monitoring, performance, and awareness of phonological variation.

nodes.label: Phonological awareness and Pinyin as a tool
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain key features of target language phonology — tones, Pinyin romanisation, homophone discrimination — and use Pinyin to support pronunciation and digital text generation.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how Pinyin represents spoken sounds and use it to check pronunciation of at least three unknown characters; identify at least two homophone pairs and explain how context distinguishes them.
nodes.typical_width: Explore the range of sounds in the target language phonological system; use Pinyin romanisation to generate digital texts; discriminate homophones; practise tongue twisters; use dictionaries and digital tools to check pronunciation; prepare a mock lesson about Chinese phonology for beginners.
wider: Research the relationship between Pinyin and spoken standard target language — explain what Pinyin captures and what it does not, and discuss its usefulness for different types of learners
Compare own pronunciation with standard spoken target language using recordings — identify systematic differences and discuss their origin (regional accent, family variety, etc.)
nodes.hinge_reason: Phonological awareness including Pinyin use is the prerequisite for all deliberate pronunciation development. Entry students with home fluency but limited phonological analysis cannot systematically monitor or improve their spoken production.

response_modes.reason: Phonological analysis requires students to examine features of language they have always used implicitly. Explicit instruction on the phonological system — tones, initials, finals, Pinyin conventions — builds the analytical awareness before students can self-monitor.

success_criteria: Explains how Pinyin represents spoken sounds and uses it to check pronunciation of at least three characters
Identifies at least two homophone pairs and explains how context distinguishes them

nodes.label: Self-monitoring and accent awareness
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare their own speech patterns with standard spoken target language, identify differences, and make targeted adjustments to pronunciation and fluency.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare own speech with at least one model of standard spoken target language, identify at least two specific differences, and demonstrate a targeted improvement attempt.
nodes.typical_width: Compare own Chinese speech patterns with Modern Standard Chinese — in news broadcasts or other formal spoken models; identify subtle pronunciation differences including regional accent features; practise adjustments; recognise and describe regional accent variation.
wider: Conduct a systematic self-review comparing recorded speech with a standard model — categorise differences and design a targeted practice plan for the most significant
Research the regional accent features of own family or community variety — describe the specific phonological patterns and explain their geographic origin

response_modes.reason: Pronunciation self-monitoring requires repeated comparison cycles — record, compare, identify, practise, re-record. Regular structured self-review activities build the reflective practice that produces genuine pronunciation development.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students bring home variety pronunciation that may differ systematically from standard forms. Width investment here builds explicit awareness of the relationship between home variety and standard — validating both while developing conscious code-switching capacity.
success_criteria: Compares own speech with a standard model and identifies at least two specific differences
Demonstrates a targeted improvement attempt for at least one identified difference

nodes.label: Performance and fluency in formal contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform target language texts — poems, speeches, formal presentations — with attention to rhythm, tone, stress and emotional expression for a specific audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Perform at least one target language text demonstrating deliberate attention to tone, rhythm or stress for communicative or emotional effect.
nodes.typical_width: Perform Chinese poems with attention to rhythm, voice, emotion and gesture; prepare and rehearse speeches with Chinese-speaking family or community members; perform for specific audiences; use intonation and stress deliberately to convey meaning.
wider: Perform a classical target language poem or literary text — explain the prosodic choices made and how they serve the text's meaning
Compare own performance of a text with a published recording — identify specific prosodic differences and evaluate the effect of each

response_modes.reason: Performance integrates phonological awareness (node 1) and self-monitoring (node 2) into a full communicative act. The teaching investment is in creating genuine performance conditions — real audiences, real texts — where prosodic control serves communicative and artistic purpose.

success_criteria: Performs a target language text demonstrating deliberate attention to at least one prosodic feature
Can explain the prosodic choice made and its intended effect
